parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, black-box, Cargo project, /output/test19.rs, CLI parsing, geometry, and byte-identical output requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent did early probing, then split work into an implementation child and a reference-fuzzing child, retaining final cross-verification and delivery review itself.
parallel.implementation: The implementation child wrote a full earcut port, a root test19.rs entry point, and Cargo.toml, then fixed a z-hash sort_linked panic found by n >= 40 tests.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child wrote directly into /output while the reference child wrote /tmp/test19_ref; the parent later checked the produced files and executable.
parallel.verification: Child tests covered fixed numeric and special args, and the parent compared the Rust binary against 83 generated oracle stdout files with zero local mismatches.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator later found one failing testcase. The visible process gap is that the parallel delegated acceptance surface omitted very large numeric argv behavior.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, black-box, CLI, geometry, output formatting, Cargo project, and /output/test19.rs requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main actor owned implementation, integration, build, edge-case exploration, verification, and final delivery without subagent handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote Cargo.toml, src/earcut.rs, and test19.rs, using an atoi-like parser that it later checked against large numeric input behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor kept one implementation tree and delivered the expected root entry file, binary, and Cargo build output.
serial.verification: It compared ordinary cases, z-hash threshold cases, special argv strings, a huge numeric argument, and n=5000 against the C++ binary, all byte-identical.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is visible at closure, and the current official evaluation passed all 38 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same top-level prompt obligations, including CLI equivalence and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and pursued byte-identical CLI and output behavior in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The divergence is not in the original prompt but in how the parallel child acceptance scope narrowed argv testing after delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent split implementation and reference fuzzing across two child agents, while the parent kept final checking.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor kept all implementation and checking work in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a parent-child task brief boundary for acceptance coverage; serial had no such handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent gave the implementation child a detailed algorithm spec and a mandatory finite verification list, and gave the reference child a separate finite oracle list.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor carried its own accumulated edge-case observations into later verification, including huge numeric argv behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel boundary omitted the very large numeric argv case from both child scopes, while serial did not lose that acceptance concern across a handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel implementation child wrote an atoi function that clamps decimal accumulation to i32::MAX and states overflow is irrelevant for its inputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial implementation used an atoi-like parser and then tested a huge numeric argument against the reference binary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel code path exposed a large-numeric argv risk that its local checks did not cover; serial's implementation was verified on that specific class.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Both child results returned to the parent and the parent inspected and used them before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child-result lifecycle; the main actor directly used its own build and test outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing join or unused result occurred; the only material lifecycle effect is that the accepted returned test corpus constrained what the parent checked.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child wrote the final /output project while the reference child wrote oracle files under /tmp/test19_ref; the parent later inspected the deliverables.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote a single /output project tree and did not coordinate shared writes with children.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision or artifact contamination is evidenced; the shared-state difference did not explain the official discordance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel accepted zero mismatches over 83 child-generated reference outputs and then finalized.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial tested ordinary values, z-hashing sizes, special strings, huge numeric argv, and n=5000 before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's acceptance set included a very large numeric argv case that the parallel acceptance set lacked.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout after one swarm and 24 tool calls, then the official evaluator found one failing testcase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout after one main trajectory and 8 tool calls, then the official evaluator passed all testcases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The pair is not explained by timeout or resource exhaustion; both closed normally, with serial having stronger edge-case verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official evaluator is serial-only pass: parallel completed at 37/38, serial completed at 38/38. The concrete process difference is that the parallel parent delegated implementation and oracle generation with finite acceptance lists that did not include a huge numeric argv case. The implementation child then wrote an atoi stand-in with overflow behavior treated as irrelevant for its inputs, and the parent accepted the artifact after the child-generated corpus passed. The serial trajectory explicitly compared huge numeric argv behavior before final delivery.
parallel_contributors: The parent-child implementation brief narrowed verification to fixed ordinary and prefix-parse arguments and did not include very large numeric argv behavior.
The implementation child wrote a clamping atoi path and documented overflow as irrelevant for the delegated inputs.
The parent accepted 83 generated reference comparisons, all of which passed, without adding the large numeric argv check later seen in serial.
serial_contributors: The serial actor tested a huge numeric argument, along with other argv variants and n=5000, before declaring completion.
The serial artifact passed the current completed official evaluator with 38/38.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The visible code-level difference is argv overflow handling; the official record does not expose the exact failing testcase, so this is recorded as the supported comparative contributor rather than a proven unique hidden case.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
